claim: *Discovering latent models in an existing system.* Weak signals identify candidate locations, not prescribed remedies. Repeated concepts worth modeling gain explicit representations; consumers migrate to them, and narrower checks can enforce selected obligations. Each pass leaves a stronger basis for subsequent recovery.
topology: Existing codebase flows through weak signals to Partition findings. Three branches lead to Legitimate shape then Accept/exempt; Latent concept then Name the model, Typed vocabulary/Explicit relations, Migrate consumers, Narrower enforcement, and Stronger model substrate; Mechanical debt then Codemod. A smooth next-pass return connects stronger substrate to existing codebase. It does not return to the weak-signal detector.
required_terms: primitive density · repeated shapes component / boundary view
bw_encoding: Only Latent concept and Stronger model substrate use light gray, identifying a model concept discovered and the substrate reinforced. All other nodes remain white. The unboxed key explains this role.
redesign: Author-requested redraw moves the latent-concept branch to the center and connects the full recovery sequence to a curved next-pass loop returning to the existing codebase. Weak-signal findings are partitioned into legitimate shapes, latent concepts, and mechanical debt. A small unboxed key explains the two gray model-related nodes. Internal heading and caption are omitted.
alt: Weak signals from an existing codebase—primitive density, repeated shapes, component/boundary view—locate potential work. Findings are partitioned into three paths: legitimate shape is accepted or exempted; mechanical debt is handled by codemod; latent concept leads to naming a model, defining typed vocabulary and explicit relations, migrating consumers, and narrower enforcement using types, lints, and a drift guard. A stronger model substrate then feeds the next pass over the existing codebase. Only latent concept and stronger model substrate are shaded.
